evidence_items.summary: Choosing a network architecture for zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs of inference needs a circuit-cost estimate that can be checked against the prover, yet NAS work on ZK has relied on untested cost proxies. We study ezkl, a Halo2-based prover, on CIFAR-10 MLPs, CNNs and ResNet-style networks. (1) Cost model. A parametric model of assigned cells, with coefficients fitted on 180 trained, calibrated networks and evaluated on 54 held-out ones, matches ezkl-calibrated logrows exactly for 39 and within one for 51 (Spearman 0.84; cross-validated over all 234 networks: 70% exact, 95% within one). The mismatches have a mechanism: on 72 dumped ezkl settings, logrows is exactly the maximum of four resource requirements (rows, constants, lookup table, range-check table; 72 of 72 sampled networks at logrows 19–23), of which cell count is one. (2) A negative result. Width-matched, ReLU and x² networks have the same calibrated logrows (all 5 skeletons; 45 of 50 matched pairs in the sweep), contradicting the assumption that polynomial activations are cheaper to prove in ezkl; unnormalized x³ + x networks calibrate to a circuit up to 16× larger at equal cell count because their range-check table spans 2²² + 1 values. (3) Benchmark. We release zkml-bench, 474 networks with two training seeds and proxy scores. NEAR predicts accuracy only for ReLU networks (ρ = +0.70) and is indistinguishable from zero on all three polynomial families; a Zen-style score (our variant, not the published Zen-Score protocol) is anti-correlated on polynomial networks; a sign-pattern NASWOT variant is negatively correlated on polynomial networks; ZiCo’s apparent success on x³ + x disappears once failed training runs are removed. Between 39% and 60% of polynomial networks fail to train. (4) Search.
evidence_items.title: ZK-Circuit-Aware NAS: A Cost Model, Benchmark, and Proxy Study for Provable Inference

evidence_items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) now generate patches, call tools, retrieve context, and iterate on test feedback, yet published gains are usually reported as counts of patches that pass a test suite on public benchmarks. This review asks whether retrieval-augmented and agentic designs yield more independently correct repairs at comparable cost. Journal articles issued from 2022 to 2026 were retrieved from the OpenAIRE Graph and Crossref with the full Boolean string, supplemented by title screening where abstracts were unavailable. A three-layer design combined a bibliometric map of 151 articles, an abstract-level evidence map and technical appraisal of 67 core empirical studies (11 in full text), and a structured synthesis of matched within-study contrasts. Output grew from 19 articles in 2024 to 83 in 2026, concentrated in five software engineering venues. Coupling analysis separated learning-based repair, agentic repository-level repair, and patch-validity research, with weak modularity indicating a shared intellectual base dominated by Defects4J. Agents, retrieval, and repository-level tasks rose sharply between 2024-2025 and 2026, whereas attention to contamination and patch correctness stayed flat. Only 11% of core abstracts mentioned the plausible versus correct distinction and 11% addressed contamination. Seven studies yielded ten matched contrasts; the nine with magnitudes showed relative gains of 6% to 56%, but none reported paired discordant outcomes or variances, so no pooled estimate was defensible. Memorization and production evidence indicate that benchmark gains overstate deployable correctness. The review proposes a minimum reporting set built on paired per-bug outcomes, budget parity, independent oracles, and contamination audits.
evidence_items.title: A bibliometric review, systematic evidence synthesis, and structured quantitative synthesis of retrieval-augmented and agentic large language models for software repair

evidence_items.summary: Bertsimas and Dunn report in Machine Learning (2017) optimal classification trees, OCT and OCT-H, benchmarked against CART on what the paper describes throughout, in its abstract and in Sections 1 and 5, as 53 UCI datasets. Every full-results table in the paper prints 54 datasets. The additional row is Optical-recognition, and it is a row in name only: every summary aggregate the paper reports, in Tables 6, 8, and 12, reproduces exactly, to printed precision, when Optical-recognition is excluded, and none of them reproduces when all 54 printed rows are used. The discrepancy is consistent across both methods and all four depths, and Optical-recognition is the unique single row whose removal restores agreement. The paper's text and summaries therefore describe a 53-dataset benchmark while its results tables print a 54th dataset whose numbers enter no reported aggregate. Either the row or the summaries need correction.
evidence_items.title: One Dataset Too Many: The Fifty-Fourth Row in the Benchmark Tables of Bertsimas and Dunn

evidence_items.summary: Children's earliest years are a period of intense social learning, during which meaning is built through gaze, gesture, and physical contact. Yet, this critical aspect of social interaction remains under-evaluated in multimodal video understanding, as existing benchmarks prioritize the conversation-driven interactions of adults. We address this gap with \bench ($\textbf{N}$aturalistic $\textbf{E}$arly-childhood $\textbf{S}$ocial in$\textbf{T}$eractions), the first child-centric benchmark for nonverbal social reasoning. \bench comprises \totalvids manually annotated clips ($\sim$12s) curated for diversity across naturalistic settings, cultural contexts, and developmental stages. Beyond a lack of data, targeted model improvement in this domain is hindered by coarse evaluation schemas that conflate basic perception with higher-order reasoning. To resolve this, \bench introduces a compositional schema that builds atomic interaction cues into progressive levels of social reasoning: contextual, behavioral, interpersonal, and open-ended descriptions. Extensive analysis of state-of-the-art Vision-Language Models (VLMs) reveals a stark performance collapse: despite strong contextual recognition, models exhibit substantial gaps in decoding precise behavioral and interpersonal cues. We trace these failures to specific biases, including poor consequence grounding and temporal sensitivity. Finally, we ground \bench in real-world applications by evaluating VLMs using domain adaptation strategies. Ultimately, \bench provides a rigorous testbed for advancing socially grounded artificial intelligence in early childhood. Project page: https://laubravo.github.io/nest_website/.
evidence_items.title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood

evidence_items.summary: This paper presents a review of the second LoViF Challenge on Real-World All-in-One Image Restoration. The challenge aims to advance unified image restoration under diverse real-world degradation conditions, including blur, low-light, haze, rain, and snow. It provides a common benchmark for evaluating the restoration accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability of models across multiple degradation categories within a unified framework. The competition attracted 158 registered participants, and 20 teams were included in the final ranking after their submitted results were successfully reproduced and verified. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of the submitted solutions and corresponding results, highlighting recent advances in real-world all-in-one image restoration. The summarized methods and empirical findings reveal effective design strategies and establish an updated benchmark for future research in real-world low-level vision.
evidence_items.title: The Second LoViF 2026 Challenge on Real-World All-in-One Image Restoration: Methods and Results

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities when trained within executable runtime environments, notably excelling at software engineering tasks through verified feedback loops. Yet, scalable and generalizable execution-grounded environments remain scarce, limiting progress in training more capable ML agents. We introduce CTF-Dojo, the first large-scale executable runtime tailored for training LLMs with verifiable feedback, featuring 658 fully functional Capture-The-Flag (CTF)-style challenges containerized in Docker with guaranteed reproducibility. To enable rapid scaling without manual intervention, we develop CTF-Forge, an automated pipeline that transforms publicly available artifacts into ready-to-use execution environments in minutes, eliminating weeks of expert configuration traditionally required. We trained LLM-based agents on just 486 high-quality, execution-verified trajectories from CTF-Dojo, achieving up to 9.9% absolute gains over strong baselines across three competitive benchmarks: InterCode-CTF, NYU CTF Bench, and Cybench. Our best-performing 32B model reaches 31.9% Pass@1, establishing a new open-weight state-of-the-art that rivals frontier models like DeepSeek-V3-0324 and Gemini-2.5-Flash. By framing CTF-style tasks as a benchmark for executable-agent learning, CTF-Dojo demonstrates that execution-grounded training signals are not only effective but pivotal in advancing high-performance ML agents without dependence on costly proprietary systems.
evidence_items.title: Training Language Model Agents to Find Vulnerabilities with CTF-Dojo

INTEGRATED QUANTUM-NANO HONEYCOMB SUSTAINABLE CIVILIZATION FAMILY 40 / F196-F200 | SCIENTIFIC & TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK | RESEARCH WORKING EDITION v1.0 33 x STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW RESEARCH LIBRARY This final research family does not claim that civilization-scale autonomy is achievable today. Five separate prospective questions are tested: practical quantum computing in nanorobotic manufacturing; independently qualified factoryless honeycomb repair; safe services for sustainable habitats; resource ledgers with a physical human stop; and cross-laboratory reproducibility of a whole-system future research benchmark. The point of the book is to leave a testable door, not an unfalsifiable promise. No figure in this edition is an observed quantum speedup, tested nanofactory, occupied habitat, or licensed civic infrastructure. THE FIVE SOURCE-ANCHORED FLAGSHIPS F196 | Integration of Quantum Computing and Nanorobotic Swarm Manufacturing at the Limit | 量子計算與奈米機器人集群製造整合的極限 F197 | Integration of Honeycomb Self-Regeneration and Factoryless Production at the Limit | 蜂巢自主再生與無工廠生產融合的極限 F198 | Quantum–Nano Robotics for Sustainable Living Civilizations at the Limit | 量子奈米機器人與永續居住文明協同的極限 F199 | Resource Circularity and Trustworthy Autonomy in Regenerative Civilization Platforms at the Limit | 自動再生文明資源閉環與可信自主平台的極限 F200 | Future Research on Quantum Honeycomb Autonomous Regenerative Civilizations at the Limit | 量子蜂巢自動再生永續文明未來研究的極限 THE FORTY-FAMILY COUPLING FRAMEWORK AND SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE Families 1-8 provide local coordination and distributed manufacturing concepts; families 9-16 introduce quantum, nanoscale and programmable materials hypotheses; families 17-24 test honeycomb architectures, repair, energy, water and ecological regeneration; families 25-32 add independent habitability, food, materials, microgrids, public services, disaster recovery and digital-twin witnesses; families 33-40 examine quantum assistance, nano-honeycomb materials, regenerative manufacturing, urban infrastructure, resource optimization, trustworthy governance, human-robot co-evolution and final integration. These are interfaces for testing, not certificates that one domain validates another. A service certificate must not travel across domains without evidence. An accepted robotic joint cannot certify drinking water; a functioning water service cannot demonstrate civil rights; a signed permission token cannot prove the motor stopped; and a quantum solver returning a good score cannot prove nanomanufacturing advantages. The architecture is meaningful precisely because these distinctions are separately recorded and falsifiable. FIVE-STAGE PARALLEL RESEARCH CONTROL SYSTEM 1 / Freeze research DNA: lock five official F196-F200 titles, the 915-page mother-work conceptual chapter lineage, distinct physical endpoints, system safety envelopes, classical strong controls and human authority constraints. 2 / Formalize mechanisms: connect 30 dimensioned candidate relations to testable material and service endpoints; generate 42 deterministic synthetic 3D response tables with CSV, Python and full parameters, not fabricated field observations. 3 / Reconstruct independent witnesses: for each chapter use calibrated physical acceptance, blind quality tests, full material and energy ledgers, confirmed human permission and reproducible timestamps; clearly separate a virtual test from a real one. 4 / Challenge competing worlds: include equal-budget classical quantum-comparison baselines, conventional repair networks, human-operated sustainable habitats, public auditing and counterfactual resource accounting. Every research door must permit a negative result. 5 / Audit and permit transfer: check engineering dimensions, figure recomputation, text layout, independent chapter progression, distinctive research gates and prototype stop tests before publication; successors may discard unsupported claims. SOURCE LINEAGE AND EVIDENCE CEILING The supplied 915-page SWARM MANUFACTURING AND ROBOTIC MATTER AT THE LIMIT research mother provides conceptual chapters 17 (Task Allocation Without a Central Foreman), 45 (Scaffolded and Scaffold-Free Construction), 63 (Self-Repairing Robotic Structures), 64 (When the Product and the Factory Become the Same System), 65 (Construction Swarms in the Built Environment), 66 (Disaster-Zone Fabrication and Repair), 71 (Infrastructure Maintenance by Distributed Agents), 73 (Scaling Laws for Million-Agent Manufacturing), 75 (Energy Economics of Distributed Production), 77 (Digital Twins for Multi-Robot Manufacturing), 79 (Standards, Interoperability, and Handoff), 81 (Robotic Matter as Civilizational Infrastructure) and 82 (Toward a Manufacturing Ecology of Autonomous Matter). The mother is not evidence that the five novel hypotheses have passed independent experiments.

The observable endpoint is independently verified explanation inconsistency [fraction]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is a transparent fixed-rule decision list with readable reasons, compared at matched latency and information budgets. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is polished post-hoc language that does not track actual model dependencies, leaked proxy labels or instrument errors. This programme never merges explanation quality, physical authority, unknown-state rejection, human decision control and trace completeness into a single achievement score. Instead, it keeps five separate operational contracts, native units, an independent validation budget and hard stop boundary. An engineering conclusion is to be withdrawn or restricted for an explanation faithfully endorses a prohibited command, the record hides unreported counterexamples, or an output is applied to a person. The Daoist warning against treating a verbal account as the whole way motivates skepticism toward an explanation; it does not certify the model. The admissible nonclinical bench is galvanically isolated dry-run controller with inert resistive loads, hardwired inhibit relay, permit simulator and independent voltage/current logger. The observable endpoint is verified physical stop latency [ms]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is hardwired interlock under human supervision with no learned policy in the permission path. This programme never merges explanation quality, physical authority, unknown-state rejection, human decision control and trace completeness into a single achievement score. Instead, it keeps five separate operational contracts, native units, an independent validation budget and hard stop boundary. Restraint and proportion are ethical prompts from acupuncture traditions; authorization is a modern operational contract, not a philosophical permission. The admissible nonclinical bench is sealed synthetic bioelectric and robotic-state replay with sensor swaps, blinded drift periods and a disabled physical-output line. The observable endpoint is OOD missed-detection fraction [fraction]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is fixed range checks and a calibrated classical distance or energy-score detector under matched false-alarm budget. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is dataset shortcut, hidden-label leakage, unmodeled cross-sensor shift or false security from a miscalibrated uncertainty score. This programme never merges explanation quality, physical authority, unknown-state rejection, human decision control and trace completeness into a single achievement score. Instead, it keeps five separate operational contracts, native units, an independent validation budget and hard stop boundary. An engineering conclusion is to be withdrawn or restricted for the human cannot refuse, a simulated veto fails its external trace, misleading consent cues remain, or any clinical superiority is inferred. The relation between responsibility, timely attention and restraint can be discussed through East Asian philosophy without reifying it into a medical efficacy claim. F040 — Trace integrity and reproducible negative cases Three-coupling: versioned evidence genealogy × independent sensor and authorization ledger × cross-laboratory adverse-case replay. The admissible nonclinical bench is synthetic end-to-end autonomous controller workflow with independent clocks, permission service, dummy load and immutable event packaging. The observable endpoint is independent event-trace completeness [fraction]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is simple append-only signed audit records plus independent bench instrumentation and manual forensic reconstruction. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is unlogged local actions, timestamp editing, selective case deletion, invalid replay assumptions or cryptographic integrity mistaken for physical truth. CAUSAL AI FOR ACUPUNCTURE 第七家族|針灸 AI 因果推論・道可道,非常道・研究之門 FAMILY 07 / F031–F035 / SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK Authors: 33 × STARLI  |  Research Working Edition v1.0  |  15 November 2026 30 candidate formulas • 42 recomputable synthetic 3D models • 82 chapters × 6 progressive stages • 200 Research Gates • 33 Phoenix prototypes PROSPECTIVE NONCLINICAL RESEARCH. No new patient experiment, placebo effect, clinical acupuncture benefit, discovered meridian electric field, autonomous needling approval or quantum advantage is asserted. Numerical figures are synthetic and cannot be used to infer biological effect sizes. Five official family flagships / 正式中英文研究題名 F031 | Causal Identification of Acupuncture-Induced Bioelectric Changes at the Limit / 針灸刺激與生物電變化因果辨識極限 F032 | Placebo and Signal Confounding Separation in Acupuncture at the Limit / 針灸安慰效應與訊號混雜分離極限 F033 | Counterfactual Validation of Acupuncture AI Models at the Limit / 針灸 AI 模型反事實驗證極限 F034 | Multivariable Causal Network Reconstruction in Acupuncture at the Limit / 針灸多變因因果網絡重建極限 F035 | Causal Safety Assurance for Autonomous Acupuncture at the Limit / 針灸自主控制因果安全保證極限 The family integration and five distinct causal objects F031 — Causal identification of electrical responses Three-coupling: controlled surrogate stimulus × independent bioelectric voltage witness × intervention-versus-artifact identification. The admissible nonclinical bench is isolated saline or conductive-gel phantom, coded electrical pulses, independently powered differential voltmeter, optical placement reference and fully disconnected clinical pathways. The observable endpoint is externally measured stimulus-attributable voltage contrast [mV]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is randomized source-on/source-off differences and a circuit-equivalent linear regression with equal calibration budget. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is shared-ground pickup, electrode polarization, timestamp drift and heating driven by the source circuit rather than a separate biological mechanism. This programme does not combine five incomparable endpoints into one achievement score. Instead, it retains their exact intervention semantics, physical unit ledger, blinded validation budget and stop boundary. A causal conclusion is to be withdrawn or restricted for loss of electrical isolation, undefined intervention dose, uncalibrated voltage reference, nonpositive overlap or any proposal to apply the bench result to a person. A named acupoint or meridian supplies a historically meaningful question; neither is a separately established physical electric-field entity. F032 — Expectation proxies and measurement confounding Three-coupling: explicit expectation and context proxy × negative-control measurement × causal confounder sensitivity. The admissible nonclinical bench is synthetic deidentified event tables and nonliving signal phantoms with simulated expectancy labels; no induced placebo response or new human intervention. The observable endpoint is unexplained confounding-adjusted response contrast [mV]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is predeclared context-only model, calibrated blinded source-off condition and negative-control analysis. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is expectation-label leakage, channel gain drift, attention-dependent missingness, assessor knowledge and correlated electrode changes. This programme does not combine five incomparable endpoints into one achievement score. Instead, it retains their exact intervention semantics, physical unit ledger, blinded validation budget and stop boundary. A causal conclusion is to be withdrawn or restricted for unverifiable placebo labels, unmeasured common cause admitted as proof, data privacy violation, source-off negative control failure or clinical extrapolation. The role of attention and ritual is a source of inquiry in traditional practice, not evidence that simulated expectation causes patient benefit. F033 — Counterfactual model validation and off-policy limits Three-coupling: frozen potential-outcome estimand × positivity-aware off-policy evaluation × sealed counterfactual simulation witness. The admissible nonclinical bench is versioned synthetic structural-causal simulator with withheld perturbation seeds and an isolated inert stimulus source. The observable endpoint is absolute effect-estimation error on sealed synthetic truth [mV]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is simple outcome-regression, stabilized inverse-propensity weighting and zero-effect or randomized-source oracle cases. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is positivity violations, propensity overfitting, post-treatment feature leakage and a simulator favoring the candidate algorithm. This programme does not combine five incomparable endpoints into one achievement score. Instead, it retains their exact intervention semantics, physical unit ledger, blinded validation budget and stop boundary. A causal conclusion is to be withdrawn or restricted for zero intervention overlap, undefined potential outcomes, unbounded importance weights, hidden test-label access or use as clinical decision policy. An unspoken alternative future echoes the question of what language omits; counterfactual quantities remain analytical constructs rather than Daoist cosmology. F034 — Identifiability of multivariable causal graphs Three-coupling: time-resolved signal network × independently induced source perturbation × graph-edge falsification. The admissible nonclinical bench is electrically isolated multichannel phantom and seeded synthetic directed acyclic graph with controlled common-source perturbations. The observable endpoint is false-directed-edge fraction on known synthetic interventions [1]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is sparse lagged regression, fixed known circuit diagram and deliberately acausal correlation network. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is latent common causes, clock misordering, feedback cycles treated as DAGs and regularization artifacts posing as directed edges. This programme does not combine five incomparable endpoints into one achievement score. Instead, it retains their exact intervention semantics, physical unit ledger, blinded validation budget and stop boundary. A causal conclusion is to be withdrawn or restricted for causal sufficiency assumption fails without sensitivity bounds, physical feedback ignored, unstable edge direction or lack of an independent perturbation. Interdependence in Chinese philosophy can inspire network questions; a graph arrow requires operational interventions rather than analogy. F035 — Causal authorization, refusal and fail-closed autonomy Three-coupling: counterfactual action-impact audit × independent physical output inhibition × human authority and safety interlock. The admissible nonclinical bench is guarded nonclinical isolated stimulation emulator with dummy impedance load, hardwired inhibit relay, independent shunt current sensor and logged veto clock. The observable endpoint is measured unwanted electrical output after veto [mJ]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is fixed-rule fail-closed watchdog and a supervised safe-state controller under matched intervention and latency budgets. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is an accurate causal model masking unsafe actuation, unrecorded capacitor discharge, permission replay or post-intervention collider selection. This programme does not combine five incomparable endpoints into one achievement score. Instead, it retains their exact intervention semantics, physical unit ledger, blinded validation budget and stop boundary. A causal conclusion is to be withdrawn or restricted for any unauthorized pulse, missing physical current witness, failed hardwired inhibit, prospective human stimulation or a causal safety claim outside the certified bench. Restraint is an ethical and cultural prompt; real safety requires physical stop evidence and explicit human authorization, not a Daoist slogan.

evidence_items.summary: Raw multi-view (MV) and multi-view multi-light (MVPS) images of the four archaeological objects shown in the paper Integrating Multi-view Multi-light Surface Reconstruction into Cultural Heritage Workflows (ECCV 2026 Workshops, VISART). For each object, a multi-view set (single illumination, for photogrammetry) and a multi-light set (several viewpoints, each imaged under several illuminations, for photometric stereo) are provided as Nikon RAW files (NEF, 45.7 MP). The dataset is intended for 3D reconstruction, multi-view photometric stereo, digital archaeology and cultural heritage studies. The Meshroom pipeline templates that process it (the method used in the paper for each object, and alternative photometric stereo methods), the installation instructions and the tested software versions are maintained in the companion repository: github.com/bbrument/mvml-heritage-meshroom . Objects Warrior ( warrior/ ) – head of a Cypriot warrior, terracotta, 6th century BC (Musée Saint-Raymond, Toulouse). Gourdan bone ( gourdan bone/ ) – engraved bone from the Gourdan cave (Gourdan-Polignan, Haute-Garonne). Biface ( biface/ ) – lithic flint biface (private collection of Benjamin Coupry, co-author). Calathos ( calathos/ ) – woman with a calathos, ceramic, 4th century BC (Musée Saint-Raymond, Toulouse). Content Object MV images PS viewpoints × illuminations PS images Lens PS lighting Warrior 121 13 × 8–10 114 35 mm Hand-held flash Gourdan bone — (all-LED image of each viewpoint, in PS/ ) 23 × 36 (35 LEDs + all LEDs) 828 50 mm macro RTI LED dome Biface 162 12 × 13 (12 LEDs + all LEDs) 156 50 mm macro 12-LED lighting rig Calathos 48 6 × 36, 1 × 106, 1 × 29 351 50 mm macro RTI LED dome ( PS 01 – PS 07 ), hand-held flash ( PS 08 ) Structure Two archives per object, [object] MV.zip and [object] PS.zip ; the Gourdan bone has only gourdan bone PS.zip .

ACUPUNCTURE DIGITAL TWINS 第五家族|針灸多模態感測・證據與可反駁之問 FAMILY 05 • F021–F025 • SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK Five official flagships · 30 candidate research formulas · 42 synthetic 3D sensitivity models · 82 progressive chapters · 200 Research Gates · 33 Phoenix research prototypes Authors: 33 × STARLI / White Rainbow Era  |  Research Working Edition v1.0  |  15 November 2026 EVIDENCE STATUS: Prospective, nonclinical, falsifiable and reproducible. No human treatment, needle insertion, device authorization, quantum advantage or clinical recovery is shown. Traditional acupuncture, Daoism, yin–yang, qi and meridian philosophy are treated as cultural and interpretative traditions, not as independently demonstrated new SI physical fields. Five official fifth-family flagships F021 | Skin–Tissue Digital Twins for Acupuncture at the Limit / 針灸皮膚組織數位孿生極限 F022 | Electric-Field Digital Twins for Acupuncture at the Limit / 針灸電場分布數位孿生極限 F023 | Mechanical Contact Digital Twins for Acupuncture at the Limit / 針灸機械接觸數位孿生極限 F024 | Individual Parameter Inversion for Acupuncture at the Limit / 針灸個體參數反演極限 F025 | Trustworthy Validation of Acupuncture Digital Twins at the Limit / 針灸數位孿生模型可信驗證極限 The dual-book architecture F021 — Skin–tissue geometric twins Core three-coupling: layered finite-element geometry / independently tracked deformation / material-batch transfer with bounded uncertainty. Physical bench: calibrated silicone-gel multilayer soft-tissue phantom with optical fiducials, ultrasound thickness reference and finite-element forward model. Strong baseline: frozen analytical elasticity or calibrated nonadaptive finite-element model evaluated on the same sealed geometry lots. Primary endpoint: held-out material geometry forecast error [mm]. Critical rival: nonidentifiable elastic moduli, camera drift, adaptive mesh leakage, changing contact boundary and post-hoc geometry fitting. Noncompensable stop: missing independent fiducial, unbounded deformation, parameter nonidentifiability, numerical nonconvergence or any patient-directed inference. Geometry, electric potential, contact force, latent material coefficients and independent validation have distinct physical references and units. A digital twin cannot qualify itself; each model must be challenged by a sealed material lot and a fair conventional physics rival. The falsifiable claim is transferred from one laboratory to another only after physical scale, reference identity, data selection, external event time, software version and valid authorization are declared. The source lineage may motivate a new hypothesis, but the assertion must survive a separate experiment. F022 — Electric-field forward twins Core three-coupling: isolated source waveform / calibrated conductive boundary conditions / independent potential-map validation. Physical bench: nonliving layered conductive hydrogel with isolated low-power source, calibrated voltmeter array and guarded current-return path. Strong baseline: frozen quasistatic resistor-network solver or analytical Laplace-model comparator with identical material and measurement budgets. Primary endpoint: held-out electrical potential-map residual [mV]. Critical rival: electrode polarization, leakage path, conductivity heterogeneity, ground-loop artefact and inaccurate boundary current. Noncompensable stop: lost electrical isolation, source compliance mismatch, unreferenced field scale or simulated field interpreted as a biological meridian. Geometry, electric potential, contact force, latent material coefficients and independent validation have distinct physical references and units. The falsifiable claim is transferred from one laboratory to another only after physical scale, reference identity, data selection, external event time, software version and valid authorization are declared. The source lineage may motivate a new hypothesis, but the assertion must survive a separate experiment. F023 — Mechanical contact twins Core three-coupling: contact constitutive dynamics / independent load-displacement metrology / passive mechanical safety bounds. Physical bench: inert textured gel phantom with robotic indentation disabled for humans, certified force cell, optical displacement and passive stop. Strong baseline: frozen Hertz-contact or Kelvin–Voigt spring-damper reference calibrated under the same loads and phantoms. Primary endpoint: held-out contact-force forecast residual [N]. Critical rival: unmodeled adhesion, friction transition, viscoelastic memory, surface roughness and shaft flexion. Noncompensable stop: force or travel exceeding predeclared phantom envelope, missing passive stop, divergent contact fit or clinical extrapolation. Geometry, electric potential, contact force, latent material coefficients and independent validation have distinct physical references and units. A digital twin cannot qualify itself; each model must be challenged by a sealed material lot and a fair conventional physics rival. The falsifiable claim is transferred from one laboratory to another only after physical scale, reference identity, data selection, external event time, software version and valid authorization are declared. F024 — Individual-parameter inverse twins Core three-coupling: identifiability-aware inverse modeling / independent reference excitation / regularized posterior uncertainty and refusal. Physical bench: library of anonymized synthetic parameterized gel phantoms with hidden material coefficients, calibrated mechanical/electrical stimuli and sealed reference labels. F025 — Trustworthy twin validation Core three-coupling: frozen validation envelopes / independent laboratory replication / negative-case lineage and noncompensable human authority. Physical bench: sealed cross-laboratory nonclinical twin benchmark combining independent optical, electrical, force and material reference artifacts. Strong baseline: preregistered classical model and simple calibrated control evaluated under equal held-out, compute and measurement budgets. Primary endpoint: independent negative-case reconstruction fraction [1]. Critical rival: shared training/test specimens, reference contamination, selective reporting, cherry-picked geometry and common-cause calibration errors. evidence_items.summary: Summary Internal multiple elimination (IME) is a challenging task in seismic exploration. If internal multiples (IMs) are not eliminated, they may be misinterpreted as primaries, leading to imaging artifacts. Among the few available methods, Marchenko multiple elimination (MME) is the most appealing, as it is data-driven and requires no model information. However, the computational cost is considerable due to the extensive calculations of multidimensional convolution and correlation, which include forward and inverse fast Fourier transforms among shot gathers. Moreover, its application to field data remains limited, indicating that more attention should be paid to practical issues. Starting from the PyMarchenko MME, a GPU-accelerated IME technique, GPU-MME, to alleviate the computational burden of MME is developed. GPU-MME faithfully replicates the PyMarchenko MME results and delivers a significant acceleration—up to nearly two orders of magnitude faster—due to the GPU’s efficiency in handling the key computations involved in MME. GPU-MME is applied to a series of synthetic datasets and an open field dataset to demonstrate its effectiveness and practical value. The comparison results are either provided or reproduced from existing work. GPU-MME is competitive with a state-of-the-art MME method. The impact of key parameters in GPU-MME and how to determine their optimal values are investigated. When accurate surface-free and wavelet-free reflection response is unavailable, an estimation of multiple and source (EMS) technique can successfully eliminate surface-related multiples (SRMs) and provide the surface-free, wavelet-free input for GPU-MME. However, additional scaling of reflection response and adaptive adjustment of the initially estimated IMs may be necessary to ensure effective IME. The scaling and adjustment procedures are discussed in detail, as they are critical when an exact reflection response is not available.
evidence_items.title: Marchenko-type GPU-accelerated internal multiple elimination (GPU-MME): Practical aspects, benchmark synthetic and field data applications

evidence_items.summary: Large language models increasingly operate over long multi-turn interactions, where behavioral stability matters as much as single-answer correctness. We study the detection of behavioral anomalies—abrupt shifts in persona, topic, style, or use of context, independent of factual accuracy—from response embeddings and, for the predictive detector, embeddings of incoming user messages, without anomaly labels, external knowledge, or reference outputs; detectors are trained only on normal dialogues and calibrated on clean data. We release a reproducible primary benchmark of 700 multi-turn dialogues generated with Mistral-7B-Instruct—100 per anomaly type—together with cross-generator replications generated with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (139 dialogues) and Qwen3-8B (310 dialogues), plus matched six- and twenty-exchange corpora that vary conversation length. The benchmark spans four controlled anomaly types, clean controls, a natural topic adaptation control, per-turn intervention labels, and blind audits by LLMs and humans. Under a deliberately leakage-free protocol, we compare twelve detectors in terms of ROC- and PR-AUC, per-type performance, latency, and recall at a fixed false-positive budget, with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals, multiple training seeds, and two encoders. The prediction-error + anchor fusion leads overall on the primary corpus (ROC-AUC of 0.762; PR-AUC of 0.771) and significantly exceeds the static anchor in the paired bootstrap, while no single detector leads for every anomaly type. The fusion also provides zero median latency and a 0.002 false-alarm rate under natural adaptation, where the anchor reaches 0.110. Proper change-point detectors do not beat the fusion or anchor, and lexical features remain useful for style shifts but false-alarm under natural adaptation. The context ignore construction uses user questions that require prior context, manifests visibly in 13/16 audited cases, and is detectable (best per-type ROC-AUC of 0.865).
evidence_items.title: Detecting Behavioral Anomalies in LLM Response Sequences: A Leakage-Free Benchmark and Comparative Study of Predictive, Distance, and Change-Point Detectors

evidence_items.summary: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. At the same time, the product's execution harness-including its tools, skills, and operating procedures-continues to evolve to support increasingly sophisticated interactions. These changes create two practical challenges: 1) Demand drift alters the distribution, intent, and complexity of user requests, causing a model trained once to fall behind; 2) Harness evolution requires the model to use newly introduced capabilities correctly without losing behavior that users already rely on. Periodic manual retraining is too delayed and labor-intensive for this setting. To address these challenges, we present G-CAST, a governed continual self-training system that converts daily production evidence under evolving demand and capability contracts into reward-routed, entropy-prioritized training data and governed reward evolution. Governed checkpoint transition under cumulative evaluation controls each model update, enabling the agent to learn newly introduced behaviors without sacrificing previously accepted capabilities. Experiments on a real production e-commerce agent show that G-CAST achieves stronger adaptation to newly introduced demand while better preserving previously accepted behavior compared with a strong autonomous post-training baseline. Ablations further show that both reward-routed, entropy-prioritized data orchestration and governed reward evolution are important to these gains. G-CAST is now deployed in Yuancai(http://cai.1688.com/), a B2B procurement agent on Alibaba's 1688 platform.
evidence_items.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands

evidence_items.summary: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments. We evaluate 73 handcrafted underwater, learned underwater, vision-language and general-purpose metrics against human preferences on five references: four published opinion-score sets and a new paired-comparison study. For each metric, we measure how often it selects the same image as people when comparing versions of the same scene. We further test whether simple image edits and small adversarial perturbations raise metric scores above the enhancement people preferred, and whether scores decrease as repeated generative edits add noise. Our results show that no metric consistently matches human preferences. The best worst-case Cohen's kappa over the five references is only 0.23 (Q-Align), while two raters in our study agree with a median kappa of 0.41. The widely used UCIQE often favors edits that people reject. On a Nano Banana Pro replica chain that should leave the image unchanged, only 22 of 73 scores decrease at every checkpoint, while noise grows by 2.5 times. We also introduce TrustUIQA, a benchmark that combines the human references, our study choices, the edited, attacked and generated images, and the scores of every metric on every image. The code is available at https://github.com/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA and TrustUIQA at https://huggingface.co/datasets/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA.
evidence_items.title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift

evidence_items.summary: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain. We release CANTraj, a naturalistic driving dataset pairing decoded CAN events with time-aligned GNSS trajectories (3,940 drives, 454 drivers), and CANTraj-Bench for evaluating trajectory recovery (3,675 drives, 431 drivers, 1,380 hours, 85,919 km). On 776 evaluation drives from 94 unseen drivers, we compare six re-implemented attacks and benchmark baselines under explicit information-access protocols, paired comparisons, and metrics incorporating failures. Experiments show that combining steering signals with road-network constraints yields the largest gain: With a known start and heading, adding steering to speed raises the online map filter's five-minute route recovery from 56% to 87%, with a median average displacement error of 43 m versus 921 m for map-free dead reckoning. Offline beam search recovers 88% of test routes with the heading and 81% without it. Because methods fail on different windows, we also evaluate an LLM harness that selects among candidate routes on 659 five-minute windows; its best configuration recovers 79% of routes on test and 83% on few-shot, outperforming the best baseline on test and matching it on few-shot. Data and code at huggingface.co/datasets/HenryYHW/CANTraj and github.com/WangYuHang-cmd/GPS--CAN.
evidence_items.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving

evidence_items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into SQL queries over increasingly complex databases. However, widely used benchmarks evaluate questions independently, overlooking settings where earlier queries over the same database can supply joins or calculations for a new question. We introduce HARE (History-AwaRe Text-to-SQL BEnchmark) to measure the accuracy and cost of adapting historical SQL. HARE comprises 1,600 requests derived from a fixed pool of 823 verified queries across four datasets. Annotations record which components each request preserves and which edits it requires, distinguishing whole-query adaptation from partial reuse. Our method, MEM-SQL (Memory-EMpowered Text-to-SQL), stores whole-query templates, reusable SQL blocks, and mappings from domain concepts to schema elements. MEM-SQL uses a layer only if every requirement assigned to it has a match above that layer's threshold. With On-demand Schema Linking (OSL), MEM-SQL consults the schema only when no layer qualifies or the generator judges retrieved evidence insufficient. Across six language models on HARE, mean execution accuracy rises from 37.1% for Direct Generation without history to 50.0% for MEM-SQL, with 76.6% fewer input tokens and 68.8% lower latency on average. Further analysis shows that requests reusing several verified queries remain a bottleneck, with accuracy falling from 56.7% to 29.7%, most sharply when reused components must be placed in a new query structure or combined with a shared join. Applying OSL to three other memory designs consistently reduces generation cost, while its accuracy benefit depends on the memory design. Verified history can thus make generation both more accurate and cheaper, but its value depends on the evidence retained and when the system consults the schema.
evidence_items.title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL

evidence_items.summary: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.
evidence_items.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems

evidence_items.summary: Controllable real-world video generation models can condition on a rendered graybox proxy video, which fixes layout, motion and camera. Coding agents can build such videos by reconstructing a 4D scene in Blender, yet no benchmark checks both these videos and the long, multi-shot scenes behind them. We introduce VibePrevisBench, a benchmark for 4D scene reconstruction: an agent turns a brief into an executable 4D scene and renders its proxy video. Its 242 tasks span four input kinds, including scripts, photos, continuations, and reference videos. Each delivery is scored along two evaluation dimensions. Rule-based Scene Check re-runs the code and compares the exported 4D scene with hidden ground truth facts in nine dimensions. VLM-based Screen Check asks a VLM judge whether the facts that pass can be recognized in the proxy video. We analyze the evaluation results and trajectories of 11 frontier coding agents and identify three key observations. First, multimodal understanding separates the agents, especially in understanding space and camera motion. Second, all agents seem to already master basic camera work and staging, and fail at challenging requests. Third, agents inspect their own renders but fail to correct their errors. Agents thus need better visual understanding of space and camera, explicit checks for challenging requests, and item-by-item verification of renders against the brief.
evidence_items.title: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender

STARLI · FAMILY 38 BOTANICAL SMART NANOMANUFACTURING Scientific & Technical Notebook F186–F190 | Research Working Edition | 100,000+ English words Five flagship research annotations — Zenodo-ready front matter F186 | Closed-Loop Botanical Nanoemulsification Process Control at the Limit The feedback regulation of nanoparticle size under logged shear energy flagship asks whether emulsifier adsorption kinetics, droplet breakage under specific shear and delayed feedback regulation can be separated from controller advantage caused by retrospectively tuned setpoints, raw-material differences or biased in-line sensors. Its primary candidate endpoint is absolute closed-loop particle-size deviation (nm). A rigorous design compares same material, time and energy budget with open-loop recipe and preregistered DOE controls and requires blinded offline particle-sizing plus timestamped torque, power and temperature measurements. The decisive failure condition is that the closed-loop advantage vanishes on unseen lots with frozen controller settings, independent offline size reference and equal energy budgets. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F187 | Real-Time Botanical Formulation Particle-Size Monitoring at the Limit The in-line particle-size metrology with drift-aware reference transfer flagship asks whether multi-angle scattering, probe fouling, refractive-index shift and asynchronous process sampling can be separated from apparent tracking performance arising from timestamp leakage, concentration-dependent scattering or hidden sensor recalibration. Its primary candidate endpoint is held-out in-line particle-size mean absolute error (nm). A rigorous design compares blind offline DLS or microscopy reference at synchronized aliquot times with locked pre-processing and requires second physical particle-sizing modality with traceable reference beads and blind extraction timing. The decisive failure condition is that mean absolute error exceeds the preregistered nm limit under unknown solids loading, sensor fouling and second-instrument transfer. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F188 | AI Experimental Design for Botanical Formulations at the Limit The prospective batch-constrained AI design of experiments flagship asks whether sequential acquisition, response-surface interaction, constrained exploration and supplier-lot randomization can be separated from AI advantage manufactured through data leakage, after-the-fact run selection, missing failures or unequal exploration budget. Its primary candidate endpoint is held-out design efficiency gain over frozen DOE (ratio). A rigorous design compares preregistered factorial, response-surface and Latin-hypercube DOE of identical run cost and material constraints and requires blinded prospective experiment allocation log with locked objective, acquisition trace and external verification design. The decisive failure condition is that the AI design fails to improve held-out target error per full-cost run against a matched and prespecified DOE baseline. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F189 | Botanical Nanoformulation Digital Twins at the Limit The identified process-state digital-twin prediction under unobserved batch shifts flagship asks whether mass-and-energy balance, shear-dependent dispersion, latent sensor states and calibrated process residuals can be separated from twin accuracy from future-data leakage, shared sensor bias, unidentifiable parameters or re-fitting after target observation. Its primary candidate endpoint is unseen-batch digital-twin prediction error (percent). A rigorous design compares physics-only mass-balance baseline and frozen empirical time-series model, all evaluated on external batches and requires orthogonal gravimetric and offline particle metrics under independent new-operator holdout. The decisive failure condition is that registered twin error or interval coverage fails once unseen supplier batches and uncalibrated sensor shifts enter the test. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F190 | Botanical Nanomanufacturing Quality Traceability at the Limit The event-sourced lot genealogy and recall decision verification flagship asks whether ingredient-to-batch dependency graph, process-event provenance, identity resolution and immutable audit links can be separated from inflated recall precision caused by omitted suspect batches, ambiguous material IDs or post-hoc graph cleanup. Its primary candidate endpoint is blinded batch recall correctness (percent). A rigorous design compares independent manual genealogy and frozen event-sourced traceability baseline on the same full batch registry and requires sealed lot release and mock-recall registry with independent reconciliation of every affected and unaffected batch. The decisive failure condition is that a single untraceable released material branch or a failed preregistered recall sensitivity veto invalidates quality release. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. Research position: The five flags are deliberately distinct. The historical attention to source description in Bencao Gangmu and Eastern relational thinking motivate the questions of harvest, provenance and preparation, while causal inference relies on current measurements, blind controls and independent reconstruction. The 3D plots in the research PDF are synthetic and explicitly reproducible; they are not experimental observations.

evidence_items.summary: Two concept probes can be equally accurate at predicting a concept from a language model’s hidden states while their scores contain different mixtures of the target concept and a correlated nuisance attribute. In four target–nuisance settings (two aspect sentiments in CEBaB; occupation and gender in BiasBios; Amazon review sentiment with negation, and with firstperson framing), two LLMs, and a population of concept extractors, we compare decodability with discriminant evidence: the score’s dependence on the nuisance at fixed target, and its response to input edits intended to change only the nuisance, filtered by two LLM judges and compared against placebo edits. Under correlated training data, extractors that are statistically equivalent in held-out AUROC differ up to several-fold in nuisance sensitivity in three of the four settings, and decodability is not a reliable proxy for it: their rank correlation changes sign across settings. The effect follows the probe’s training data, not the nuisance’s natural association with the target: first-person framing, unrelated to sentiment in natural reviews, is absorbed at least as much as negation, which co-occurs with negative sentiment, and decorrelated training removes the systematic effect. Selecting extractors with nuisance-aware development diagnostics, which need nuisance labels but no counterfactuals, lowers counterfactual nuisance sensitivity wherever the default choice is sensitive, at a small accuracy cost. Concept measurements should be validated, not just decoded.
evidence_items.title: Decodability Is Not Validity: Evaluating Nuisance Sensitivity in Language Model Concept Probes

evidence_items.summary: Hydrologic models, including deep learning systems now deployed for operational flood forecasting, are evaluated primarily by how closely their simulated hydrographs match observed streamflow. However, high hydrograph skill does not guarantee physical consistency: in a synthetic calibration experiment, a conceptual model that loses 15% of its water input to an unreported sink still reaches a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.93, and no shared benchmark tests whether models obey fundamental conservation laws. Here we introduce HydroTuring (v0.1.0), a black-box benchmark of 37 physics probes that test mass (24 probes), energy (7) and momentum (6) conservation in hydrologic models. Each probe runs a controlled experiment on forcing generated at run time from a recorded seed and applies binary pass or fail criteria validated against 18 physically exact and 59 deliberately broken reference models. Across 32 evaluated models (3 exact references, 7 AI-based models and 22 process-based models), only the 3 exact references pass every probe among the 28 models scored on 5 or more probes. Process-based and AI-based models pass similar shares of their scored probes (76% and 74%), and a pre-trained flood-forecasting LSTM fails 6 of the 11 runoff-only probes it can be scored on. Furthermore, 49% of all 1,184 model-probe pairs remain unscored because models omit the required state or flux variables, while the scored failures occur in perturbation responses and state bounds rather than long-term water-budget closure. HydroTuring provides a reproducible smoke test for model development, peer review and operational deployment under an open community protocol.
evidence_items.title: HydroTuring: A physics probe benchmark testing mass, energy and momentum conservation in hydrologic models

evidence_items.summary: Arabic aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) remains constrained by the limited availability, domain diversity, and task coverage of annotated resources. This study introduces AraProd-ABSA, a manually annotated Arabic dataset for fine-grained ABSA covering multiple product categories and both product-related and transaction-related aspects. The dataset contains 3154 reviews, 3204 sentences, and 4833 opinion tuples, including 4025 explicit and 808 implicit targets, annotated using an Entity#Attribute taxonomy comprising five entity types and eight attribute types. Baseline experiments were conducted on six ABSA tasks—three individual tasks and three combined tasks—using four pretrained Arabic Transformer encoders: AraBERTv0.2, MARBERT, QARiB, and ARBERT, under a common experimental protocol. The results reveal task-dependent differences among the encoders, with statistical comparisons indicating significant differences in some tasks, while other observed differences were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings provide a multi-task benchmark and reference results for future research on Arabic product-review ABSA.
evidence_items.title: AraProd-ABSA: A Multi-Category Arabic Product-Review Dataset and Benchmark for Individual and Combined Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis Tasks

evidence_items.summary: With the rapid expansion of content-centric architectures like Named Data Networks (NDN), efficient cache management has become essential for optimizing network performance. Among the various factors, the parameter β plays a crucial role in adjusting cache sensitivity based on content popularity distribution. An improper choice of this parameter can lead to lower cache hit rates, increased data pollution, and inefficient use of resources. This research introduces a novel framework utilizing the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) for distributed and adaptive tuning of β. The decentralized structure of the proposed model enables implementation at the network node level, facilitating fast convergence and accurate β tuning through coordinated updates of both primary and dual variables. Additionally, an enhanced version, ADMM-Enhanced, has been developed to offer greater stability, precision, and adaptability to network dynamics by automatically adjusting the parameters λ and ρ. To evaluate four network topologies (simple, hierarchical, enhanced, and mesh) were simulated under three operational scenarios: steady state, cache pollution attacks (CPA), and traffic load changes. Experimental results indicate that the ADMM-Enhanced algorithm increased the cache hit rate by 30% and reduced pollution to zero in stable conditions. It also demonstrated robust, adaptable, and resilient performance under severe attacks (with 30% attackers), maintaining a cache hit rate (CHR) of 18% and a cache pollution rate (CPR) of 18%. Furthermore, in complex topologies like mesh, the algorithm maintained cache efficiency and quality despite distributed threats, congestion, and link failures, showing high adaptability to dynamic network conditions.
evidence_items.title: Comparing the performance of caching algorithms in named data networks with a focus on reducing contamination attacks and optimizing the β parameter

evidence_items.summary: This repository provides the reproducibility materials for the study entitled “A Stability-Oriented Refined Compromise-Based MCDM Framework for Post-Disaster District Prioritization.” The materials support the implementation and evaluation of PURPOSE, a refined compromise-based multi-criteria decision-making framework that integrates objective subcriterion weighting, hierarchical aggregation, two-step normalization, and reference-related compromise scoring. The repository includes two post-disaster case studies in Indonesia: Donggala, Central Sulawesi, as the primary case study, comprising 16 alternatives, 30 raw subcriteria, and 19 main criteria. North Sumatra, as a cross-context replication case, comprising 19 alternatives, 43 raw subcriteria, and 17 main criteria. The computational experiments include baseline ranking, weight perturbations, normalization parameter sensitivity, alternative removal with fixed and recomputed weights, component ablations, comparison with other MCDM methods, numerical boundary conditions, and computational scalability. The North Sumatra case also includes documentary concordance with a reference ranking derived from indicative recovery action-plan funding. Files PURPOSE Publication Replication v1 1 0.zip — Final decision matrices, Python implementation, experimental configurations, validation procedures, plotting scripts, and reproduction instructions. RUN PURPOSE Publication.ipynb — Google Colab notebook for executing the computational experiments and generating the publication figures. PURPOSE Publication Reference Results v1 1 0.zip — Reference computational outputs, supporting tables, numerical validation results, and publication figures. The package supports reproduction of the reported computational results from the finalized decision matrices and the documentary funding reference.

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for translation,yet their ability to convey pragmatic meaning remains underexplored. A qualitativeanalysis grounded in speech act theory and politeness theory was applied to refusals,requests and compliment responses from high-context languages (Uzbek, Japanese)rendered into English. Translations tend to preserve propositional content but flattenindirectness, address forms and face-saving strategies, drifting toward low-contextAnglo-American directness. These patterns are interpreted as pragmatic transfer andcultural bias rooted in training-data imbalance; pragmatics-aware evaluation andprompt design are proposed.
evidence_items.title: PRAGMATIC TRANSFER AND CULTURAL BIAS IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL TRANSLATIONS OF HIGH-CONTEXT SPEECH ACTS

evidence_items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) produce literary translations that read fluently, yet fluency reveals little about whether a narrator's voice, a poem's indeterminacy, or a culturally loaded reference survives. This systematic review examined how literary quality has been defined and measured in empirical studies of LLM literary translation, how far different kinds of evidence converge, and under which conditions prompting and human revision alter the preservation of literary features in translated texts. Semantic Scholar and Crossref searches, journal-targeted queries, and citation chasing covered January 2022 to September 5, 2026, and eligibility was restricted to journal articles from Scopus-listed sources. Forty-one studies were included, 28 extracted from full texts and 13 from abstracts, and each was appraised on nine validity domains without a summed score. The evidence is concentrated on Chinese and Arabic source texts, English targets (28 studies), and GPT models (37 studies), and 28 studies relied on a single evaluation method. Accuracy and fluency often matched or exceeded published human translations, whereas narrator differentiation, culturally framed stances, symbolic references, and taboo forces were compressed or neutralized in better-controlled designs. Overlap metrics broadly agreed with expert or reader judgments in only one of the seven studies reporting both, and reader backgrounds changed rankings. Prompt effects were model-specific and sometimes traded stylistic gains for unsupported additions, while human revision appeared only in case- and practice-based designs. A five-layer evaluation framework is proposed in which claims about voice and culture require evidence at the layers they invoke, together with research priorities for Indonesian and other underrepresented literature.
evidence_items.title: Literary voice, cultural meaning, and human revision in large language model translation from 2022 to 2026

evidence_items.summary: Abstract The objective was to identify the optimal MRI sequence to evaluate postoperative Achilles tendon (AT) healing. We compared T2 gradient sequence with 4.1ms (TE4) and 16ms (TE16) echo time with PD (proton density-weighted) through signal intensity (SI) measurements and correlated them with tendon-specific biomarkers. Additionally, the study assessed agreement between radiologists and AI in evaluating tendon-specific biomarkers. A total of 45 patients (mean age 36 ± 6 years; 36 men, 9 women) underwent nine consecutive MRI examinations at intervals from 1 to 52 weeks after surgery. SI in all postoperative MRI examinations was measured in AT in TE4, TE16 and PD. SI in the operated AT appears normal in PD and TE16 sequences around week 39. However, TE4 still shows high signals, indicating ongoing remodeling. Significant correlations were found between biomarkers and SI in the TE4 sequence ( p < 0.001 for structural changes and tendon edema, and p = 0.002 for tissue edema). High SI values were associated with poor biomarker outcomes. The mean absolute errors (MAE) between AI model scores, obtained using only axial TE4 scans, and radiologist evaluations ranged from 0.12 to 0.63. In conclusion, TE4 demonstrated greater sensitivity to persistent postoperative signal and structural abnormalities and may be useful in postoperative assessment of AT. AI scores showed relatively small absolute differences from the reference radiologist scores.
evidence_items.title: Postoperative evaluation of Achilles tendon using short echo time MRI and artificial intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Background: Artificial intelligence is used to detect and characterize abnormalities in diagnostic imaging and to support clinical interpretation. Technical performance does not always translate into patient benefit. Aim: To evaluate applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in diagnostic imaging, focusing on diagnostic performance, collaboration with clinicians, and limitations of clinical implementation. Methods: To identify recent articles on the use of artificial intelligence in diagnostic imaging, the PubMed database was searched. Only English-language publications were included. Results: AI algorithms have promising capabilities for detecting and characterizing abnormalities in mammography, radiography, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and ultrasonography. In selected settings, they improve sensitivity, support segmentation, and reduce interpretation workload. However, they do not consistently improve specificity, time to intervention, or patient outcomes. The clinical evidence varies in methodological quality and representativeness. Conclusions: AI should primarily be considered a decision-support technology rather than an autonomous replacement for clinical judgment. Wider adoption requires external validation, workflow-based evaluation, and ongoing safety monitoring.
evidence_items.title: Artificial intelligence in diagnostic imaging

evidence_items.summary: Security teams increasingly rely on machine learning to detect malware and on language models and other automation to process threat intelligence. Both use cases pose the question, though: when should we trust what the system says? This paper proposes a set of trusting, explainable and trustworthy artificial intelligence in cybersecurity, including transparent detection of malware and evidence-based automated threat intelligence, that combine seven trust properties (fidelity, stability, robustness, calibration, plausibility, accountability, and security of explanations itself), compares eight families of explanation methods, shows an alert-level workflow where every explanation is verified before it impacts a decision, and describes an intelligence pipeline where every claim is tied to a source and to a technique in a standard taxonomy. It lists levels of automation for six intelligence tasks and an evaluation protocol for detection, explanations, calibration, analyst utility, extraction quality, and governance. The article describes the evidence that explanations may disagree and are unstable or manipulated, and that language model extraction of threat techniques may be highly error prone to error modes. It views explanations as an attack surface and a source of over-reliance, not just a benefit. It presents an analysis work in design and does not provide any new experimental results. Four tables and three figures show the framework concrete, and can be adopted by security operations.
evidence_items.title: Explainable and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Cybersecurity: A Framework for Transparent Malware Detection and Automated Threat Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: In response to the current predicaments faced by university English translation teaching in the era of artificial intelligence, such as narrowed goals, fixed content, monotonous models, lagging evaluation, and the absence of AI literacy among teachers and students, this study has constructed a transformation analysis framework covering five dimensions: goal positioning, content organization, teaching model, evaluation method, and teacher-student roles. Based on this framework, a four-stage process-oriented teaching model of "AI pre-translation - comparative diagnosis - post-translation editing - reflection and summary" for human-machine collaboration has been proposed. The study adopts a quasi-experimental design and implements a 12-week teaching intervention for 82 non-English major undergraduate students at a certain university. The experimental results show that the post-test translation scores and post-translation editing abilities of the experimental class are significantly better than those of the control class; at the same time, the experimental class also shows significant improvements in various dimensions of AI usage strategies, the accuracy of critical judgment, the level of intrinsic motivation, and the perception of task value. The analysis based on qualitative data further confirms the positive changes in students' awareness of strategies, repositioning of human-machine roles, and enhanced metacognitive monitoring. In summary, these findings indicate that structured human-machine collaborative training can simultaneously enhance translation quality, process strategy level, and learning motivation quality, providing an evidence-based basis and operational practical paths for the digital transformation of university English translation teaching.
evidence_items.title: Research on the Transformation of College English Translation Teaching Driven by Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Does access to transaction-level records affect which forecasting method public-finance analysts should choose? To answer this question, we compare four aggregation strategies and a structural one applied to a short, highly seasonal time series of child-benefit payments: direct-aggregate, bottom-up, data-enrichment, and minimum-trace reconciliation. Our application concerns monthly child-benefit expenditure in Republika Srpska (Bosnia and Herzegovina), where we have approximately a hundred observations of total payments, but more than a million observations of individual payments. We also consider four different ways to deal with the recurring near-zero observations typical of administrative payment data. Under an expanding-window design, where each model can only use information available at the time of each forecast origin, exponential smoothing attains the lowest error across every treatment, though once the overlapping blocks and multiple testing are accounted for, it is statistically indistinguishable from minimum-trace reconciliation and several other benchmarks. Enrichment with microdata-derived features offers no advantage once those features are restricted to information known in advance, and machine-learning methods do not outperform the benchmarks; the treatment of the near-zero observations is as consequential for measured accuracy as the choice of forecasting method. The administrative microdata nonetheless prove valuable in a different way: an entitlement-basis (accrual) series reconstructed from them is far smoother than the cash series, suggesting that their main contribution may lie in defining what is measured rather than in feeding machine-learning models; we examine this accrual view, and its limitations, in an appendix.
evidence_items.title: From Microdata to Macro Forecasts: A Comparative Study of Aggregation Strategies and Benchmark Models in Social Protection Spending

evidence_items.summary: Chatbot Arena gives each language model one Bradley-Terry score, which fixes how often any model should beat any other. Choice theory predicts where this fails: near-copies are compared on the few details in which they differ, so votes between them are more decisive than their scores imply, exactly for the comparison a lab cares about, a new version against the old one. On 1.8 million Arena votes, votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times as decisive as Bradley-Terry predicts, between sizes of one generation 1.26 times and between models of one lab 1.12 times; a release a year later points the same way, and the effect survives tie, prompt, topic and timing checks. How alike two models' answers are worded and formatted tracks the effect. Plain scores leave the odds between relatives about 9% too close to even on held-out votes; a correction with four to six parameters roughly halves this and predicts held-out votes better, mostly by modeling ties, while the leaderboard order barely moves; frozen and carried to new releases, its gains in head-to-head odds are too small for our test to establish. With language-model judges and three-answer menus, a near-copy takes votes mostly from its twin when choices are pooled over prompts (log-odds shift +0.10, 95% interval 0.05 to 0.16), less so within a prompt.
evidence_items.title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena
